spec.title: Independent rebuild: brain-wiring model predicts spread of Parkinson's-linked protein in mice, r = 0.696
spec.statement: Henderson et al. (Nature Neuroscience, 2019) modelled how alpha-synuclein, the protein linked to Parkinson's disease, spreads along the mouse brain's wiring. They report that the model's predictions match lab measurements with a correlation of 0.696 at 3 months. This re-runs an independent Python rebuild by Bourdenx and Paul (ReScience C) on the study's data. It is not the authors' own R and MATLAB code, which is also public.

source.license: MIT (replication code and data in the repository)
source.authors: Replication: M. Bourdenx, T. Paul. Original: M. Henderson et al.

setup: pip install numpy==1.26.4 pandas==1.5.3 scipy==1.11.4 statsmodels==0.14.1 matplotlib==3.8.4 seaborn==0.12.2 tqdm==4.67.1
artifact.entrypoint: python -c "import pandas as pd, runpy, Robustness_Stability as R; pd.Index._index_data = property(lambda s: s.values); R.random_robustness = lambda *a, **k: None; runpy.run_path('Pipeline.py', run_name='__main__')" > rerun_output.txt

metric.name: correlation between predicted and measured pathology at 3 months
